newsitem.title: USA: Banyan unable to pursue Apollo deal.
newsitem.headline: Banyan unable to pursue Apollo deal.

text.p: Banyan Mortgage Investment Fund said its board reviewed the latest acquisition proposal from Apollo Real Estate Advisors LP, and the company is unable to pursue further discussions at this time.

In a statement released late Thursday, Banyan said that the proposal required RGI Holdings, which agreed to merge its subsidiary RGI U.S. Holdings Inc with Banyan in April, to participate in the proposed transaction, but RGI advised that it had no interest.

Under the Apollo proposal, Apollo would have purchased newly created class B common shares. The new shares would have given Apollo up to 25 percent economic interest in the company as well as 10 votes per share and the right to elect a majority of the Banyan board.

The proposal also included the conveyance of substantially all Banyan's assets to RGI Holdings. Apollo would also pay RGI $500,000 for an option to buy one million shares of the company's stock currently owned by RGI for $1 a share, Banyan said in a December 23 release.
Banyan has received other acquisition proposals as well, including one from D. Andrew Beal, the principal stockholder of Beal Financial Corp.
